_note: Pairs of tree people who are ONE person entered twice, declared by their tree ids. Written 16 October 2026, on David's ruling relayed by the landing-site session, after an audit of this archive's pages.

A declared copy KEEPS ITS ADDRESS, because an address that has been published may have been linked or written down and deleting a row deletes it. The page says it is the same person as the primary, carries a canonical link to the primary, and is left out of the sitemap and the search index. The primary is untouched.

THE RULE FOR CHOOSING THE PRIMARY, so the choice can be audited and not only trusted: the copy that draws more of the family (marriages and children), then the one that cites more sources. Anything only the copy knows stays on the copy's own page, which still exists.

NOT declared, on purpose: the two Ralph Sneyds of 1793 (same years, DIFFERENT parents: a Keele conflation, work list 151, not a duplicate), and every pair the audit rated low (a shared parent and nothing else, which is how a family reuses a name). A declaration is evidence of identity and is made only on the strong kind: same name, same years, same parents or same children.

pairs.name: Joseph Samuel Sneyd
pairs.why: Joseph Samuel Sneyd: the tree holds him twice, as «Joseph Samuel1» and «Joseph Samuel2», with the same parents (Samuel Charles Sneyd and Catherine Margaret Mulcahy), the same birth year and the same wife, Ellen Marian Corbett. Primary: the copy that draws more of the family, 2 marriages and 12 children against 1 and 10, and cites 4 sources against 1.
